records.label: cyber
records.why: On researchers (Germany's Fraunhofer Institute for IT Security) finding that Android security apps—meant to remove viruses and warn of phishing—can themselves contain serious vulnerabilities that attackers could exploit unnoticed to disable the app's protection, spy on personal info, or even turn the app into ransomware, disclosing the flaws to developers (vulnerabilities).

records.label: cyber
records.why: An educational article on internet security—how the internet's open nature and lack of central deterrent laws enabled cybercrimes like packet sniffing, computer hacking, email virus attacks, and hoaxes—arguing internet security is an important problem to solve (amid symmetric/asymmetric encryption); an internet-security explainer (cyber).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On FireEye finding that despite Apple/Google patches for the serious 'FREAK' (Factoring attack on RSA-EXPORT Keys) vulnerability, it still threatens 1,228 Android and 771 iOS apps—a flaw letting attackers run a man-in-the-middle attack to record and decrypt weakly-encrypted SSL traffic between users and servers (vulnerability).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On Ukraine's cyber-police chief (Serhiy Demedyuk) telling Reuters that Russian hackers are targeting Ukrainian companies (banks to energy infrastructure) with malware to create 'backdoors' for a big coordinated attack—planting it from various sources to evade antivirus until activated as one unit on a set day, working with foreign agencies to track them (state cyberattack).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On WhatsApp (Facebook-owned) suing Israel's NSO Group (per BBC Arabic)—accusing it of hacking ~1,400 phones (journalists, rights activists, dissidents, diplomats in the UAE, Bahrain, Mexico) with spyware via WhatsApp servers in April/May, seeking a permanent injunction—the first such legal action by an encrypted-messaging provider (state spyware/lawsuit).

records.label: not_cyber
records.why: An auto-generated removal page for the 'FindGoFind' browser hijacker (a PUP/adware generating pop-ups, redirects, and changed search/homepage across Chrome/Firefox/IE) pushing an 'automatic removal tool'; a browser-hijacker removal-tool promo, product/scareware marketing, not cybersecurity subject matter.

records.label: borderline
records.why: An explainer warning not to trust everything online amid the boom in 'deepfakes'—AI manipulating video/audio to mimic reality—illustrated by the world's first deepfake video (Revel.ai) of Nina Shik warning that lines between reality and fiction are blurring, cryptographically signed by Truepic to flag it as AI-generated; a deepfake/AI-and-society piece (borderline).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On hackers/developers (team unc0ver) releasing the first public iOS jailbreak in a long time—working on all iPhones running iOS 11 through 13.5 by exploiting a zero-day vulnerability Apple was unaware of—breaking Apple's 'walled garden' restrictions to access the OS's core, while Apple defends its policy as protecting against spyware (zero-day/jailbreak).

records.label: not_cyber
records.why: A roundup of the best phone antivirus apps—since sites are full of viruses/malware and phones face hacking/data theft, users need protection apps from Google Play/App Store—curating the best after testing several; a security-app-recommendation piece, product roundup, not cybersecurity subject matter.

records.label: cyber
records.why: A roundup of the best 8 DNS-protection solutions (Neustar UltraDNS, Comodo Dome Shield, Cloudflare, Palo Alto DNS Security, DNSFilter)—explaining DNS as the internet's phone book, how unprotected DNS is manipulable by cybercriminals (DNS hijacking), and how DNS-protection tools defend networks against online threats (DNS-security explainer/roundup).

records.label: cyber
records.why: An explainer on the Security Operations Center (SOC)—a central place employing people/process/technology to continuously monitor and improve an organization's security posture (preventing, detecting, analyzing, and responding to cyber incidents)—detailing the SOC analyst tiers (L1/L2/L3), incident-response, threat-hunting, and digital-forensics teams (SOC explainer).

records.label: not_cyber
records.why: The terms of use for the Abdul Latif Jameel insurance-broking website (governing access/use, warranty disclaimers); a legal-boilerplate/terms piece, the 'antivirus'/'phishing'/'malware' keywords are a false positive (prohibited-use clauses).

records.label: cyber
records.why: A description of ManageEngine's Vulnerability Manager Plus—explaining what a vulnerability is (a device's security weakness attackers exploit to harm/breach privacy) and how the tool (across Windows/Linux/Mac) proactively scans for suspicious activity, assesses threat severity, and fixes/mitigates vulnerabilities on user servers; a vulnerability-management tool piece (infosec content).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On research (Germany's Security Research Labs, Karsten Nohl and Jakob Lell) finding Android phones missing some security patches are still on average safer than Windows PCs—and that some makers (ZTE, TCL worst) lied about installed patches—with SRL updating its SnoopSnitch app to show a phone's actual patch level (Android security research).

records.label: cyber
records.why: An explainer on network security (and studying it as a major)—defining it as protecting a network from unauthorized/malicious access (hacker intrusions), how wireless routers/switches auto-encrypt communications, wireless IDS/IPS, and the field's scope (data science, software engineering, AI) (network-security explainer).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On King Salman issuing a royal order establishing Saudi Arabia's National Cybersecurity Authority (its board including the State Security, General Intelligence, deputy interior minister, and defense-ministry assistant heads)—plus a definition of cybersecurity (preventing unauthorized use, ensuring systems' availability, and protecting data confidentiality/privacy) (national cybersecurity).

records.label: cyber
records.why: An explainer on Saudi Arabia's anti-cybercrime law—amid the spread of electronic hacking/info theft with the tech revolution—defining information crimes, its penalties, and the goals it achieves (protecting the national economy, achieving information security, protecting public interest/morals, and safeguarding lawful use of networks/computers) (cybercrime law).

records.label: not_cyber
records.why: A roundup of the best free PC antivirus programs (Windows)—warning some free ones bundle bloatware/slow the system, then recommending options like Bitdefender Free (background cloud scanning); a security-software-recommendation piece, product roundup, not cybersecurity subject matter.

records.label: cyber
records.why: On Palo Alto Networks/IDC research finding ~33% of UAE organizations rank cyber resilience a top priority but only 15–19% of UAE CISOs periodically test their attack-recovery plans (below the survey average)—with endpoints, networks, and cloud the top attack targets, and EDR and continuous identity verification the top security-investment areas (cybersecurity research).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On Trend Micro revealing an old Android malware ('GhostCtrl') using new tricks to turn devices into spy tools—giving hackers full control to view all phone contents and spy on users unnoticed—in three evolving versions, an offshoot of a data-stealing worm and the notorious OmniRAT, disguised as legit apps (like WhatsApp) that install a hidden malicious APK backdoor (Android spyware).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On a new generation of cyber-warriors able to stop giant container ships and cargo planes—Kaspersky's David Emm telling CNBC any digital system can be hacked (proven by a 2019 US pen-test on a Boeing plane)—noting hacking port/airport companies is often easier, e.g. Germany's Hellmann Worldwide Logistics hit by a phishing attack forcing it to disconnect its global data centers (logistics/transport cyberattacks).

records.label: cyber
records.why: An explainer on Saudi Arabia's anti-cybercrime law (Royal Decree M/17, 1428H/2007, 16 articles: definitions, aims, penalties, CITC responsibility)—framed for education (urging teachers/students to report cybercrimes like harassment, extortion, suspicious sites during remote learning), covering Article 3 crimes (impersonation, defamation, hacking, e-theft) (cybercrime law).

records.label: cyber
records.why: On a vulnerability in Netgear's popular ReadyNAS network-storage product (used by mid-size firms) that exposes network data—found and reported by Tripwire's Craig Young—patched via firmware three months prior but only some internet-connected devices updated, letting attackers exploit it, alongside related VMware/Chrome/Cisco vulnerability fixes (vulnerability).
